question: Explain why a series LCR circuit may behave as resistive, inductive, or capacitive depending on the relative values of $X_L$ and $X_C$.

options.A: If $X_L>X_C$, the circuit is capacitive and current leads voltage; if $X_C>X_L$, it is inductive and current lags.
options.B: If $X_L>X_C$, net reactance is inductive and current lags voltage; if $X_C>X_L$, net reactance is capacitive and current leads voltage; if $X_L=X_C$, the circuit is purely resistive at resonance and voltage/current are in phase.
options.C: A series LCR circuit is always resistive because all three elements are in series.
options.D: The circuit is inductive only when $X_L=X_C$ and capacitive only when $R=0$.
